mainEntity.name: How much is a home in 95304?

acceptedAnswer.text: The typical home value in 95304 is $920,793 as of 2026-09-30, down 0.07 percent from the month before and down 0.9 percent over the year. That is the Zillow Home Value Index. It estimates the typical value of every home in the area, listed or not. The median asking price of what is actually on the market in ZIP 95304 is $995,750. Those two numbers measure different populations and they do not have to agree. For one specific house instead of the typical one, that is a comparable sales analysis, and it is a different exercise than reading an index.
95304 is in ZIP 95304, Tracy, San Joaquin County, California.

Against the rest of Tracy, yes. 95304 ranks 2 of 29 neighborhoods by typical value, and at $920,793 it sits 38 percent above the citywide typical value of $668,130. The monthly number is the one I would focus on: owning the typical home here runs about $298,675 a month once you include the loan, property tax, insurance, utilities and a maintenance budget, against a typical area rent of $2,613. The full breakdown is in the cost of holding section above.

mainEntity.name: What are property taxes in Tracy?

acceptedAnswer.text: I use 1.15 percent in this report, the Tracy effective rate. On a home at $920,793 that is roughly $882 a month, $10,589 a year. Proposition 13 sets the base at 1 percent of assessed value and caps growth in that assessed value at 2 percent a year while one owner holds the property, and voter-approved bonds sit on top. The real rate runs above 1 percent. The part that catches buyers is that a purchase resets assessed value to the price paid. Any figure you read that was built from median taxes actually paid is averaging in decades of protected assessments and will understate what a new buyer owes.

mainEntity.name: What is the transfer tax in Tracy?

acceptedAnswer.text: This is the cost people forget to budget for, and it varies more by city line than anything else in a California transaction. Tracy is a general law city, so the rate here is $1.10 per $1,000 of value. On a home at $920,793 that is $1,013. For scale, the identical sale price would carry $1,013 in Escalon and $1,013 in Tracy, both in this same county. Who pays is set by the contract and by local custom, not by statute, and it is negotiable. Escrow is the authority on the exact figure for a specific sale.

mainEntity.name: What is the FHA loan limit in Tracy?

acceptedAnswer.text: For 2026 the one-unit limit in San Joaquin County is $832,750, and that figure is both the conforming conventional ceiling and the FHA ceiling. Here is why that matters in 95304. At the typical value of $920,793, a minimum-down loan would be $888,565. That is $55,815 over the ceiling. To get inside it you would need $88,043 down, about 10 percent. The most expensive home a 3.5 percent down FHA loan reaches in this county is around $862,953. This is the single most common thing I see people find out too late.

mainEntity.name: What first-time buyer help is available in Tracy?

acceptedAnswer.text: CalHFA runs the statewide programs and they layer on top of a first mortgage and do not replace it. MyHome is a deferred-payment junior loan toward the down payment and closing costs, open year round. ZIP covers closing costs on a CalHFA conventional first. Dream For All is the shared-appreciation program, limited to first-generation buyers, and it runs in announced windows, not continuously. GSFA Platinum is a separate option, and Tracy and San Joaquin County run their own programs on their own funding cycles. Those are the ones most people never hear about. The constraint that actually binds in a neighborhood at $920,793 is almost never income. It is the program's own purchase price cap, often set below the county loan limit. I would establish the price a program allows first, then shop inside it. Doing it the other way around is how people fall for a house the assistance cannot reach.

mainEntity.name: Can I build an ADU in Tracy?

acceptedAnswer.text: Almost certainly yes, in some form. State law requires local agencies to allow accessory dwelling units on residential lots with ministerial approval and a decision deadline, so the real question is what size and configuration the local ordinance permits, not whether you are allowed. Owner-occupancy requirements on new ADUs have been removed, so the main house and the ADU can both be rented. Selling one separately is a different question. Assembly Bill 1033 lets a city allow an ADU to be sold as its own condominium unit, but it is permissive and not mandatory, relatively few cities have adopted an enabling ordinance, and without one there is no right to do it. That is a question for the Tracy planning department and the municipal code, not something the state law answers on its own.

mainEntity.name: Is the Tracy housing market slowing down?

acceptedAnswer.text: I would rather give you the two numbers that disagree than a verdict. Typical home value in 95304 is down 0.07 percent month over month and down 0.9 percent year over year. Meanwhile in ZIP 95304, the median asking price is down 16.1 percent year over year, price per square foot is up 6.6 percent, active listings are up 1.3 percent month over month, and median days on market is up 29.9 percent. More supply and a slower pace sitting alongside a higher typical value is a composition effect, not a contradiction. Anyone giving you a one-word answer about a market this specific is not looking at it closely.

The Zillow Observed Rent Index for ZIP 95304 is $2,613 as of 2026-09-30, up 1.7 percent over the year. I use that figure in the cost of waiting section to show what renting while you decide actually costs over two and five years, because that is the real comparison and it usually goes unmade.

mainEntity.name: How many homes are for sale in 95304?

acceptedAnswer.text: In ZIP 95304 as of 2026-09 there were 41 active listings, up 1.3 percent from the prior month and up 92.9 percent from a year earlier. That month saw 16 new that month and 6 pending. Median days on market was 66.

mainEntity.name: How much is home insurance in Tracy?

acceptedAnswer.text: I use $215 a month, $2,580 a year, the California statewide average. A real quote on a specific house moves with the structure, the roof, the replacement cost and the wildfire risk rating on the parcel, so treat the average as a placeholder until you have a quote. One thing worth flagging: a vacant home is a different and more expensive class of policy. That catches sellers who move out before closing, and it catches estates almost every time.

mainEntity.name: What is it like living in 95304?

acceptedAnswer.text: The section near the top of this report covers what is actually here: the streets, the transit, the commercial strip and the housing stock. On the money side, typical value is $920,793, the monthly carry is around $298,675, and rent runs $2,613. I rebuild this report every month, so the figures are current to 2026-09-30 for value and 2026-09 for listing activity, not whenever the page happened to be written.
